model_enigma-m3-ukwd: Enigma M3 / M4 in M3 mode · UKW-D
model_enigma-kd: Enigma KD (FRA wiring; Mil Amt uncertain)
ukwd_wiring_hint: Enter 12 disjoint uppercase pairs separated by spaces, using every free contact exactly once. Do not enter the permanent pair. The engine receives BP notation only.
ukwd_notation_hint: German key-sheet labels omit J and Y. BP uses A–Z except the permanent B/O contacts. Changing notation converts valid wiring; invalid input is kept for correction.
search_reflector_hint: Search all 12 free pairs, keeping the permanent BP BO pair. Only hill climb supports this; partial exhaustion and crib attack are unavailable.
reflector_starts_hint: 1–1000000; default 8. More independent starts improve recovery chances but cost more time. Recovery is not guaranteed.
ukwd_cpu: Unknown UKW-D wiring runs on CPU only. GPU is selected: choose CPU explicitly to continue; no automatic fallback.
ukwd_hc: Unknown UKW-D wiring supports hill climb only, not partial exhaustion or crib attack.
ukwd_fixed: UKW-D position and ring are fixed at A/A (historical setting). KD also has a fixed A/A entry wheel and no plugboard.
ukwd_count: Enter exactly 12 wiring pairs, covering all 24 free contacts.
ukwd_pair: Each wiring pair must contain exactly two uppercase contact letters, separated from the next pair by a space.
ukwd_reused: Wiring contacts must be distinct and used once each; remove repeated or self-paired contacts.
ukwd_german_contacts: German notation uses uppercase A–Z without J or Y. The unlabeled fixed contacts must not be entered.
ukwd_bp_contacts: BP notation uses uppercase A–Z without B or O; BO is permanently wired and must not be entered.
attack_ring_hint: The ring changes the wheel's letter alignment. The left ring rarely matters: leave it known as A if unsure. Unknown rings greatly increase the search.
attack_plugboard_hint: Add only pairs you know. Each letter can have just one cable. The search can try cables between the remaining letters.
search_plugboard: Search the rest of the plugboard
search_plugboard_hint: Leave checked to look for unknown cables while keeping your known pairs fixed. Uncheck only if you know the complete plugboard.
ciphertext_hint: Paste the original message exactly. Only A–Z is accepted; nothing is removed or converted automatically. Use the uppercase button only if you want to change it.
method_hint: Hill climb improves cables step by step and is the recommended starting point. Partial exhaustion tries many initial cable pairs too, so it takes longer. Crib attack uses a known plaintext fragment on the CPU; it starts with the right ring unknown and the other rings at A, all editable below.
crib_hint: One fragment per attack. Sent exactly as typed: uppercase A–Z only, no spaces (the Enigma had no space key; operators used X). Use the button to convert to uppercase if needed.
crib_invalid_intro: These crib characters are outside A–Z (positions count from 1):
crib_position_hint: A 0-based position in the ciphertext. Leave empty to try every admissible position.
crib_short: Fewer than 14 letters: many false stops may make this slow. You can still start and cancel if needed.
bombe_cpu: The crib attack runs on the CPU only; GPU is unavailable.
seeds_hint: All tries every initial single pair and the empty board. Touching restricts those pairs to your chosen letters; use it only with a reason to narrow the search.
seed_letters_hint: Enter distinct uppercase letters without spaces, such as ABC. These letters must not belong to a known cable pair.
initial_measure_hint: How the first search recognizes promising text. Leave ic (letter repetition) to begin; language tables can help with longer messages.
final_measure_hint: How to rank the final candidates. Leave sinkov_trigram for the included German table. Other languages need your own table.
stages_hint: Extra work on the best candidates after the main search. Recommended: reswapping, then score refinement, both using sinkov_trigram. Stages run in the order shown.
stage_reswapping_hint: Tries rearranging several existing cables. Leave checked with sinkov_trigram for the recommended setup.
stage_measure_hint: Improves the remaining candidates using this stage's score. Leave checked with sinkov_trigram.
stage_trie_hint: Uses a dictionary to look for words. Leave off unless you have a matching JSON v1 dictionary file.
stage_score_hint: Leave sinkov_trigram for German. ic measures letter repetition; entropy measures letter variety. Sinkov scores compare letter groups of length 1–6 with a language table. trie looks for dictionary words and needs a dictionary file.
base_measure_hint: The score to use before dictionary refinement. Keep the previous score unless you have a specific scoring table to try.
max_pairs_hint: The total number of cable pairs allowed, including known ones. Leave empty for 13 while searching, or the known pair count when not searching.
switch_pairs_hint: Controls when the search tries switching cable pairs. Leave empty for the recommended 7 (allowed: 0–13).
backtrack_pairs_hint: Controls when the search tries removing pairs to explore another path. Leave empty for the recommended 5 (allowed: 0–13).
hold_hint: How many best candidates to retain and refine. Leave empty for 5; more candidates use more time and memory (1–1000).
threads_hint: How many CPU workers can search together. Leave empty for half your logical CPUs, at least one. A smaller value keeps your computer more responsive (1–256).
backend_hint: CPU is the default. GPU uses the graphics card for hill-climb and partial-exhaustion attacks with supported settings and never silently falls back to CPU. Resume uses the backend chosen here.
gpu_usage_hint: An integer from 1 to 100 (default 100). Lower values keep the screen smoother but take longer; results stay the same.
error_backend_unavailable: The GPU backend is unavailable. Check the engine's reason below; no CPU fallback was used.
own_table_hint: Optional for the included bigram/trigram tables; required for other language-table scores or dictionary refinement. Enter an absolute path to a JSON v1 file, not a folder.
table_format: Tables must use engine JSON v1 n-gram/dictionary format. To convert bomm txt n-grams, use e2e/recovery/ngrams.py convert. Included sinkov_bigram and sinkov_trigram tables describe German from 1941; own files override them.
estimate_hint: An approximation measured on a reference computer (Ryzen 5 2600). Your hardware, text and settings change the time. Actual elapsed time appears while running.
estimate_long: This may take over an hour. Fix more known values to reduce the search.
estimate_very_long: This may take over 24 hours! Choose more known wheels, rings or positions before starting.
distinct_wheels: Distinct wheels (as on the real machine)
distinct_wheels_hint: A real machine had one copy of each wheel. Leave checked to skip orders such as II-II-IV and search faster. Uncheck to also try repeated wheels.
error_distinct_wheels: No distinct wheel order is possible. Choose different known wheels, mark a wheel unknown, or uncheck distinct wheels.
repeated_wheels: Distinct wheels is off: unknown wheels also try repeats, such as I–I–I. These are included in the key count.
status_failed: Failed — the engine could not finish the attack.
cancel_hint: Cancellation stops at the next safe point and saves a checkpoint. It may take a while; closing the tab does not stop the attack.
partial_results: This attack was cancelled. These results are partial.
error_invalid_settings: Review the advanced settings or the path to your scoring table.
error_missing_table: This score needs an own table. Enter its full JSON v1 file path in Advanced.
error_nothing_to_search: There is nothing to search. Mark an unknown value or search the remaining plugboard.
error_attack_running: An attack is already running. Wait or cancel it before starting another.
error_attack_not_running: There is no running attack to cancel.
error_attack_not_resumable: This attack has no resumable checkpoint.
title: Enigma
subtitle: A local machine for encrypting and decrypting messages
path: Full path to the Enigma engine
path_hint: Built from source? Look for target/release/enigma inside the project folder. Installed elsewhere? Run which enigma on Linux/macOS or where enigma on Windows to print its location. Enter the full path to the file, not the folder. Only choose a program you trust: saving runs it to check its version.
engine_missing: No engine saved yet. Enter its full path above to begin.
blocker: First connect a compatible Enigma engine above. Your machine settings and message will stay here.
machine_intro: Use the same settings to encrypt and decrypt. Each Start begins again at your chosen positions.
model_hint: The model determines which wheels and reflectors you can use. Enigma M4 has an extra Greek wheel.
reflector_ring_hint: Reflector ring setting, separate from its initial position. Railway and G have no plugboard; their entry wheel is fixed at A/A.
reflector_position_hint: Initial reflector position. Railway's reflector stays still; G's reflector moves during encryption. Unknown searches all A–Z positions.
reflector_hint: The reflector sends the signal back through the wheels. Choose the same one used for the original message.
wheel_hint: Each wheel has different wiring inside. The order matters: match each slot to the original settings.
ring_hint: The ring changes the alignment of the letter markings with the wheel's wiring. It is separate from the starting position; copy both from the message settings.
position_hint: This is the letter visible in the window before you start. The windows here show only those initial settings, not the moving wheels.
plugboard_hint: A cable swaps two letters before and after the wheels. Each letter can belong to just one pair; leave this empty if there are no cables.
pair_invalid: Choose two letters from A to Z.
pair_reused: One of those letters already has a cable. Remove that pair first.
text_hint: Only uppercase A–Z is accepted, with no spaces or accents. Nothing is changed or sent while you type. Empty text is also allowed.
invalid_text_intro: Nothing was sent. These characters are outside A–Z (positions count from 1):
uppercase_done: Converted to uppercase. Review the message, then press Start; any remaining symbols still need your attention.
copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the result and copy it manually.
lamps_hint: The lit lamp shows only the last letter of the result. No wheel movement is displayed.
error_not_absolute: Enter the full path, starting at the root of your drive, not a relative path.
error_not_found: No file was found at that path. Check the location and spelling.
error_not_executable: Choose an executable file, not a folder. It must have permission to run.
error_not_enigma: That program did not identify itself as the Enigma engine. Choose the Rust enigma executable.
error_unsupported_version: This engine is not compatible. Found: {found}. Supported: {supported}.
error_timeout: The engine took too long to respond. Check the executable and try again.
error_invalid_request: The request could not be read. Review your settings and try again.
error_internal_error: The local server could not read or save its settings. Check its terminal for details and try again.
error_engine_not_configured: Save an engine path above before starting.
error_engine_incompatible: The saved engine is no longer compatible. Check and save its path above again.
error_engine_failed: The engine could not complete the message. Check its executable and try again.
error_unknown_model: Choose one of the available machine models.
error_invalid_component: One of the machine settings is not available for this model. Review the wheels, letters and cable pairs.
error_invalid_text: The engine rejected the message because it contains a character outside its alphabet.
engine_error_invalid_json: The engine could not read the request format.
engine_error_invalid_request: The engine could not accept this request.
engine_error_unsupported_version: The engine does not support this request's protocol version.
engine_error_unknown_field: The request contains an option the engine does not recognize.
engine_error_invalid_definition: The machine definition is not valid.
engine_error_invalid_symbol: One of the configured letters is not valid.
engine_error_invalid_wiring: The machine's internal wiring is not valid.
engine_error_invalid_reflector: The reflector setting is not valid.
engine_error_invalid_plugboard: The cable pairs are not valid.
engine_error_invalid_slot: One of the wheel settings is not valid.
engine_error_invalid_rule: One of the machine's movement rules is not valid.
engine_error_invalid_search_space: The engine rejected the range of settings.
engine_error_unsupported_job: The engine does not support this operation.
engine_error_unsupported_pass: The engine does not support this search method.
engine_error_unsupported_measure: The engine does not support this scoring method.
engine_error_unsupported_resource: A requested engine resource is not supported.
engine_error_invalid_text: The message contains a character outside the machine's alphabet.
engine_error_unsupported_topology: The engine does not support this arrangement of wheels.
engine_error_resource_limit: The request exceeds the engine's limits.
engine_error_internal_error: The engine encountered an internal problem while processing the message.
error_unauthorized: This session is not connected. Open the full link printed in the server terminal again.
error_network: Could not reach the local server. Make sure enigma-web is still running and try again.
error_generic: The local server could not complete the request. Try again.
